#!/usr/bin/python3
"""External model watchdog for the jadegate mayor session (Afik's order, 2026-09-07 17:33 CST,
#gastown 1788773614): the mayor must run Fable. If it is downgraded (Opus, Sonnet, anything else),
post an alert in #gastown, mail the mayor telling it to hand off to a fresh Fable session, and post
again when it is back on Fable.

Signal: Claude Code writes every assistant turn to the session transcript
(~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl) with a "model" field. That is what the harness actually
used for the turn -- it does not depend on the session noticing or reporting its own model, which is
exactly what failed on 2026-09-07 (three hours on Opus with "Opus 5" in the session's own prompt).
The mayor's transcript is the one gc itself names: `gc session list --json` carries the Claude session uuid
(`session_key`) of the session with alias "mayor", gc launches claude with `--session-id <that uuid>`, and the
transcript file is <uuid>.jsonl (jg-074ur3, 2026-09-20). Only when gc cannot answer does it fall back to the
most recently modified transcript whose head opens a paragraph with the mayor system prompt.

Second verdict, STALLED (2026-09-20, DO-NOT 137): the newest assistant rows are ALL API-error rows
(`isApiErrorMessage`), i.e. every turn is dying before a model answers -- an org that disabled Claude Code
access, a usage wall, or any other API error. On 2026-09-20 05:19-07:03 CST that went unseen for 1 h 44 min
because error rows are (rightly) skipped when reading the model. Same alert path as DOWNGRADED; the
watchdog changes nothing in cswap or the settings for it (DO-NOT 74). ORG-DISABLED and WALL are never
transient and stall at ONE trailing error row; any other API error needs K (default 2). A stall is only
called Resolved on two trailing real rows, or one real row that has stood for 10 minutes (jg-074ur3).

Runs from launchd (com.jadegate.model-watchdog) every 5 minutes. Stdlib only.

  mayor-model-watchdog            # normal tick: classify, alert/resolve on transitions, log
  mayor-model-watchdog --status   # print current model + state, change nothing
  mayor-model-watchdog --dry-run  # classify and print what would be posted/mailed, send nothing
  mayor-model-watchdog --announce # post a one-line "armed" notice to #gastown (used once)
  mayor-model-watchdog --model-only  # print just the model id (used by bin/mayor-heartbeat)
"""
import calendar, glob, json, os, re, subprocess, sys, time, urllib.request

HOME = os.path.expanduser("~")
PROJECT_DIR = os.path.join(HOME, ".claude/projects/-Users-tailor64s-macbook-pro-city")
MAYOR_MARKER = b"You are the mayor of this Gas City workspace"
# The real prompt opens a paragraph with the marker ("# Mayor\n\nYou are the mayor..."; "\n" is the two
# characters backslash-n inside a JSONL row). The pinned memory mayor-must-run-fable-5-1 QUOTES the marker
# and is loaded into every session of this project, pool workers included, so a bare substring test took
# the newest pool worker's transcript for the mayor's (seen 2026-09-20 07:39 CST: a worker's own
# transcript was classified) -- which would also hide a stalled mayor behind a healthy worker.
MAYOR_MARKER_RE = re.compile(rb"(?:\\n|\n)" + re.escape(MAYOR_MARKER))
STATE = os.path.join(HOME, "city/.heartbeat/model-watch.json")
LOG = os.path.join(HOME, "Library/Logs/mayor-model-watchdog.log")
SLACK_ENV = os.path.join(HOME, ".config/gc-slack-adapter/env")
GASTOWN = "C0ASAPRETDK"
AFIK = "U0AN32RPBFT"
REQUIRED_PREFIX = "claude-fable"
SETTINGS = os.path.join(HOME, ".claude/settings.json")
FABLE_SETTING = "claude-fable-5-1[1m]"   # what the field must read (Afik 2026-09-09 12:37: "let it restore the field")
FLAG_KEY = "switchModelsOnFlag"          # Claude Code auto-switch to Opus on a safety-flagged turn (default true); Afik 12:37: "those should be disabled"
REALERT_SECS = 60 * 60          # while still downgraded, repeat alert + mail hourly
HEAD_BYTES = 200_000            # how much of a transcript to scan for the mayor marker
TAIL_BYTES = 2_000_000          # how much of the tail to scan for recent model fields
MODEL_RE = re.compile(rb'"model":"([^"]+)"')
BAD_STATES = ("DOWNGRADED", "STALLED")
STALL_ROWS_DEFAULT = 2          # newest K assistant rows all API errors = STALLED; env WATCHDOG_STALL_ROWS overrides
STALL_TEXT_CHARS = 160
CSWAP = os.path.join(HOME, ".local/bin/cswap")
GC = os.path.join(HOME, ".local/bin/gc")
CITY = os.path.join(HOME, "city")
MAYOR_ALIAS = "mayor"
GC_SESSION_SECS = 10            # bound on the read-only `gc session list --json`
SESSION_KEY_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{8}(?:-[0-9a-f]{4}){3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$")
DETERMINISTIC_SIGS = ("ORG-DISABLED", "WALL")   # never transient: STALLED at ONE trailing error row (mayor's ruling 2026-09-20)
RESOLVE_REAL_ROWS = 2           # a stall is Resolved on this many trailing real rows ...
RESOLVE_QUIET_SECS = 10 * 60    # ... or on one trailing real row that has stood this long with no error after it
_SELECTED = {"by": None}        # which rule picked the transcript this run (shown by --status)


def log(msg, stream=None):
    line = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S ") + msg
    print(line, file=stream or sys.stdout)
    try:
        with open(LOG, "a") as f:
            f.write(line + "\n")
    except OSError:
        pass


def gc_mayor_session_key():
    """Claude session uuid gc records for the mayor session: `session_key` of the one open session with
    alias "mayor" in `gc session list --json`. gc picks that uuid itself and launches claude with
    `--session-id`, so it follows every gc handoff and never depends on prompt text. Read-only, bounded to
    GC_SESSION_SECS; raises on any failure (the caller falls back)."""
    out = subprocess.run([GC, "session", "list", "--json"], cwd=CITY, capture_output=True, text=True,
                         timeout=GC_SESSION_SECS, check=True).stdout
    sessions = json.loads(out).get("sessions") or []
    mayors = [s for s in sessions if isinstance(s, dict) and s.get("alias") == MAYOR_ALIAS and not s.get("closed")]
    if len(mayors) != 1:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{len(mayors)} open gc sessions with alias {MAYOR_ALIAS!r}")
    key = mayors[0].get("session_key")
    if not isinstance(key, str) or not SESSION_KEY_RE.match(key):
        raise RuntimeError(f"mayor session_key is not a uuid: {key!r}")
    return key


def find_mayor_transcript():
    # Primary: the session gc says is the mayor's. Nothing that sniffs prompt text may come first -- every
    # session of this project quotes the marker sentence through the pinned memory.
    try:
        path = os.path.join(PROJECT_DIR, gc_mayor_session_key() + ".jsonl")
        if not os.path.isfile(path):
            raise RuntimeError(f"gc names {os.path.basename(path)}, which is not in the project dir")
        _SELECTED["by"] = "gc-session"
        return path
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 -- a hung or missing gc must never hide the verdict
        # stderr: --status and --model-only own stdout
        log(f"GC-SESSION-FAIL {type(e).__name__}: {e}; falling back to the prompt-marker rule", sys.stderr)
    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(PROJECT_DIR, "*.jsonl")), key=os.path.getmtime, reverse=True)
    loose = None
    for f in files:
        try:
            with open(f, "rb") as fh:
                head = fh.read(HEAD_BYTES)
        except OSError:
            continue
        if MAYOR_MARKER_RE.search(head):
            _SELECTED["by"] = "paragraph-start"
            return f
        if loose is None and MAYOR_MARKER in head:
            loose = f
    _SELECTED["by"] = "substring" if loose else None
    return loose  # no paragraph-start match anywhere (prompt reworded?): the old substring rule beats UNKNOWN


def assistant_rows(path):
    """Assistant rows of the transcript tail, oldest first, as ("real", model, ts, None) or
    ("error", None, ts, text).

    Parses JSONL rows and looks only at rows with type == "assistant" (never regex-scans raw text, so an
    error row quoted inside a tool result is not an error row). An error row is one flagged
    isApiErrorMessage. A real row carries a Claude model id. Everything else -- the harness placeholder
    "<synthetic>" WITHOUT the error flag (reminder/resume turns, the 2026-09-08 shape), non-Claude ids --
    is dropped: it is neither a model reading nor an error.
    """
    size = os.path.getsize(path)
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        fh.seek(max(0, size - TAIL_BYTES))
        tail = fh.read()
    lines = tail.split(b"\n")
    if size > TAIL_BYTES and lines:
        lines = lines[1:]  # first chunk may be a partial row
    rows = []
    for raw in lines:
        if b'"assistant"' not in raw or (b'"model"' not in raw and b'"isApiErrorMessage"' not in raw):
            continue
        try:
            e = json.loads(raw)
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if not isinstance(e, dict) or e.get("type") != "assistant":
            continue
        msg = e.get("message") if isinstance(e.get("message"), dict) else {}
        ts = e.get("timestamp") if isinstance(e.get("timestamp"), str) else None
        if e.get("isApiErrorMessage"):
            rows.append(("error", None, ts, _row_text(msg)))
            continue
        m = msg.get("model")
        if not isinstance(m, str) or m == "<synthetic>" or not m.startswith("claude-"):
            continue
        rows.append(("real", m, ts, None))
    return rows


def _row_text(msg):
    content = msg.get("content")
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content
    if isinstance(content, list):
        return " ".join(b.get("text", "") for b in content if isinstance(b, dict) and isinstance(b.get("text"), str))
    return ""


def recent_models(path, n=20):
    """Models of the last n REAL assistant turns.

    Parses JSONL rows and reads message.model only from rows with type == "assistant"; ignores the
    harness placeholder "<synthetic>" (written on reminder/resume turns with no model output -- the row that
    tripped citadel's watchdog 2026-09-08 00:38Z), rows flagged isApiErrorMessage, and any model string that
    is not a Claude id. Never regex-scans raw text: a "model":"..." literal inside a tool result or a pasted
    config would otherwise be read as the mayor's own model (Afik 2026-09-08: "just fix the watchdog").
    """
    return [m for kind, m, _, _ in assistant_rows(path) if kind == "real"][-n:]


def stall_threshold():
    try:
        k = int(os.environ.get("WATCHDOG_STALL_ROWS", ""))
    except ValueError:
        return STALL_ROWS_DEFAULT
    return k if k >= 1 else STALL_ROWS_DEFAULT


def stall_signature(text):
    if "disabled Claude subscription access" in text:
        return "ORG-DISABLED"
    low = text.lower()
    # "out of usage credits" (2026-09-09, the consent-fallback class) has no "limit" and is just as deterministic;
    # a transient "rate limit" 429 is not a wall and keeps K (mayor's rulings 2026-09-20, jg-sewnrh)
    if "usage credits" in low or ("limit" in low and "rate limit" not in low):
        return "WALL"
    return "API-ERROR"


def _epoch(ts):
    try:
        return calendar.timegm(time.strptime(ts[:19], "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def trailing_errors(rows):
    """The run of API-error rows at the newest end of the tail (nothing real after them), or None."""
    run = []
    for row in reversed(rows):
        if row[0] != "error":
            break
        run.append(row)
    if not run:
        return None
    run.reverse()
    text = " ".join((run[-1][3] or "").split())
    sig = stall_signature(text)
    return {
        "signature": sig,
        "count": len(run),
        # An org that disabled access and a usage wall do not clear by themselves: one dead turn is enough.
        # On 2026-09-20 the mayor's turns were an hour apart, so K=2 would have alerted an hour into the outage.
        "threshold": 1 if sig in DETERMINISTIC_SIGS else stall_threshold(),
        "first_ts": run[0][2],
        "last_ts": run[-1][2],
        "first_epoch": _epoch(run[0][2]),
        "text": text[:STALL_TEXT_CHARS],
    }


def recovery_confirmed(rows, path, now=None):
    """True when a stall may be called Resolved: the newest RESOLVE_REAL_ROWS assistant rows are all real,
    or the newest row is real and has stood RESOLVE_QUIET_SECS with no error after it. One real row between
    errors is not a recovery (an intermittently failing seat would flap Resolved / STALLED)."""
    if not rows or rows[-1][0] != "real":
        return False
    newest = rows[-RESOLVE_REAL_ROWS:]
    if len(newest) == RESOLVE_REAL_ROWS and all(r[0] == "real" for r in newest):
        return True
    born = _epoch(rows[-1][2])
    if born is None:
        born = os.path.getmtime(path)   # never earlier than the row, so this only waits longer
    return (time.time() if now is None else now) - born >= RESOLVE_QUIET_SECS


def settings_model():
    try:
        with open(SETTINGS) as f:
            return json.load(f).get("model", "(unset)")
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return f"(unreadable: {e})"


def classify(prev_state=None, prev_stall=None):
    """prev_state / prev_stall: the saved verdict, so a STALLED verdict is HELD until the recovery is
    confirmed (recovery_confirmed). Without them the reading is stateless, as before."""
    path = find_mayor_transcript()
    if not path:
        return {"state": "UNKNOWN", "reason": "no mayor transcript found", "model": None, "transcript": None}
    rows = assistant_rows(path)
    models = [m for kind, m, _, _ in rows if kind == "real"][-20:]
    stall = trailing_errors(rows)
    stalled = bool(stall) and stall["count"] >= stall["threshold"]
    if not models and not stalled:
        return {"state": "UNKNOWN", "reason": "no model fields in transcript tail", "model": None, "transcript": path}
    # A session that STARTED on a dead seat has error rows and no real row at all: that is STALLED, not
    # UNKNOWN -- staying silent there would repeat the 2026-09-20 incident after any handoff onto such a seat.
    current = models[-1] if models else None
    if current is not None and not current.startswith(REQUIRED_PREFIX):
        state = "DOWNGRADED"            # precedence: a non-Fable last real turn wins over the error run
    else:
        state = "STALLED" if stalled else "OK"
    held = state == "OK" and prev_state == "STALLED" and not recovery_confirmed(rows, path)
    if held:
        state = "STALLED"               # one real row between errors keeps the verdict
    c = {
        "state": state,
        "model": current,
        "recent": models,
        "transcript": os.path.basename(path),
        "transcript_mtime": int(os.path.getmtime(path)),
        "settings_model": settings_model(),
        "selector": _SELECTED["by"],
    }
    if stall:
        c["stall"] = stall              # shown by --status even below the threshold
    if held:
        c["held"] = True
        if not stall:                   # nothing trailing: the alert texts keep the facts of the stall being held
            c["stall"] = dict(prev_stall) if isinstance(prev_stall, dict) else _unknown_stall()
    return c


def _unknown_stall():
    return {"signature": "API-ERROR", "count": 0, "threshold": stall_threshold(), "first_ts": None,
            "last_ts": None, "first_epoch": None, "text": ""}


def load_state():
    try:
        with open(STATE) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        return {}


def save_state(s):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(STATE), exist_ok=True)
    tmp = STATE + ".tmp"
    with open(tmp, "w") as f:
        json.dump(s, f, indent=1)
    os.replace(tmp, STATE)


def _load_settings():
    with open(SETTINGS) as f:
        raw = f.read()
    return raw, json.loads(raw)


def _save_settings(d, raw, label):
    """Back up the current file beside it, then write atomically and read back. Raises on any failure."""
    backup = SETTINGS + ".bak-wd-" + time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S") + "-" + label
    with open(backup, "w") as f:
        f.write(raw)
    tmp = SETTINGS + ".wd-tmp"
    with open(tmp, "w") as f:
        json.dump(d, f, indent=2)
        f.write("\n")
    os.replace(tmp, SETTINGS)
    with open(SETTINGS) as f:
        json.load(f)
    return backup


def restore_settings_model(dry=False):
    """Put ~/.claude/settings.json's model back to Fable when it is not (Afik's order 2026-09-09).

    Claude Code itself rewrites the field on a `model_consent_fallback` (seen 2026-09-09 02:16:12Z:
    "Fable 5.1 requires usage credits", choice switch_default, answered by queued input). A running
    session keeps its model until it hands off, so this only guarantees the NEXT session comes back
    on Fable; the mail tells the mayor to hand off. Returns (changed, old_value, backup_path). Never raises.
    """
    try:
        raw, d = _load_settings()
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        log(f"RESTORE-FAIL read {SETTINGS}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        return (False, None, None)
    old = d.get("model")
    if isinstance(old, str) and old.startswith(("claude-fable", "fable")):
        return (False, old, None)
    if dry:
        print(f"WOULD RESTORE settings.json model {old!r} -> {FABLE_SETTING!r}")
        return (True, old, None)
    try:
        d["model"] = FABLE_SETTING
        backup = _save_settings(d, raw, "model")
        back = _load_settings()[1].get("model")
        if back != FABLE_SETTING:
            raise RuntimeError(f"read-back shows {back!r}")
        log(f"RESTORED settings.json model {old!r} -> {FABLE_SETTING!r} (backup {os.path.basename(backup)})")
        return (True, old, backup)
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        log(f"RESTORE-FAIL write {SETTINGS}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        return (False, old, None)


def enforce_settings_flags(dry=False):
    """Keep `switchModelsOnFlag` false (Afik 2026-09-09: disable any auto-downgrade setting; citadel has it
    false since 9/3 and re-asserts it every tick, so both copies match). Idempotent; never raises."""
    try:
        raw, d = _load_settings()
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        log(f"FLAG-FAIL read {SETTINGS}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        return False
    old = d.get(FLAG_KEY)
    if old is False:
        return False
    if dry:
        print(f"WOULD SET {FLAG_KEY}=false (currently {old!r})")
        return True
    try:
        d[FLAG_KEY] = False
        backup = _save_settings(d, raw, "flag")
        if _load_settings()[1].get(FLAG_KEY) is not False:
            raise RuntimeError("read-back still not false")
        log(f"ASSERTED {FLAG_KEY}=false (was {old!r}; backup {os.path.basename(backup)})")
        return True
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        log(f"FLAG-FAIL write {SETTINGS}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        return False


def slack_token():
    """Bot token from the environment or the adapter env file.

    The adapter file writes `export SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=...` (since 2026-08-22); the original
    `startswith("SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=")` never matched it, so every real alert from 2026-09-07 to
    2026-09-09 died here with RuntimeError before anything was logged (30 tracebacks in the
    launchd log across both downgrades). Accept both the bare and the `export` form, and quotes.
    """
    tok = os.environ.get("SLACK_BOT_TOKEN", "").strip()
    if tok:
        return tok
    with open(SLACK_ENV) as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.strip()
            if line.startswith("export "):
                line = line[len("export "):].lstrip()
            if line.startswith("SLACK_BOT_TOKEN="):
                val = line.split("=", 1)[1].strip().strip('"').strip("'")
                if val:
                    return val
    raise RuntimeError("SLACK_BOT_TOKEN not found in env or " + SLACK_ENV)


def slack_post(text, dry=False):
    if dry:
        print("WOULD POST to #gastown:\n" + text)
        return True
    body = json.dumps({"channel": GASTOWN, "text": text, "unfurl_links": False}).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        "https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage", data=body,
        headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + slack_token(), "Content-Type": "application/json; charset=utf-8"},
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=20) as r:
        res = json.load(r)
    if not res.get("ok"):
        raise RuntimeError("slack: " + str(res.get("error")))
    return res.get("ts")


def mail_mayor(subject, body, dry=False):
    if dry:
        print("WOULD MAIL mayor:\nSUBJECT " + subject + "\n" + body)
        return
    subprocess.run(
        [os.path.join(HOME, ".local/bin/gc"), "mail", "send", "mayor", "--notify", "-s", subject, "-m", body],
        cwd=os.path.join(HOME, "city"), timeout=90, check=False,
    )


def alert_text(c, first):
    head = "*MODEL DOWNGRADE on the jadegate mayor*" if first else "*jadegate mayor still downgraded*"
    r = c.get("restored")
    if r and r.get("changed"):
        fix = f"settings.json restored to Fable by the watchdog (was `{r.get('old')}`)."
    elif r and r.get("old") is not None and not r.get("changed") and str(r.get("old")).startswith(("claude-fable", "fable")):
        fix = "settings.json already says Fable."
    else:
        fix = f"settings.json model `{c['settings_model']}` -- restore FAILED, see the watchdog log."
    return (
        f"{head} <@{AFIK}> -- the mayor's last turn ran on `{c['model']}`, not Fable. "
        f"Transcript `{c['transcript']}`. {fix} "
        "The mayor has been mailed to hand off to a fresh Fable session now."
    )


def mail_text(c):
    r = c.get("restored") or {}
    if r.get("changed"):
        fix = f"The watchdog has restored settings.json to {FABLE_SETTING} (it read {r.get('old')!r}; backup kept), so a handoff now comes back on Fable."
    elif str(c["settings_model"]).startswith(("claude-fable", "fable")):
        fix = "settings.json already says Fable, so a handoff should come back on Fable."
    else:
        fix = f"settings.json model is `{c['settings_model']}` and the watchdog could NOT restore it (see ~/Library/Logs/mayor-model-watchdog.log) -- fix the file, then hand off."
    return (
        f"Your last turn ran on {c['model']}, not Fable 5.1 (transcript {c['transcript']}). "
        "Afik's rule (memory mayor-must-run-fable-5-1): STOP starting rounds, dispatches and outbound messages. "
        f"{fix} Then run: gc handoff \"HANDOFF: model downgrade, restarting on Fable\" \"<current context>\" "
        "-- the first line of the handoff body must tell the next session to verify it is on Fable 5.1 and to re-arm crons from crons/registry.jsonl. "
        "This mail repeats hourly until the transcript shows Fable again; #gastown has been alerted and will be told when it is resolved."
    )


def resolved_text(c, since, prev="DOWNGRADED"):
    mins = int((time.time() - since) / 60) if since else 0
    if prev == "STALLED":
        return (
            f"*Resolved: jadegate mayor is completing turns again* (`{c['model']}`, transcript `{c['transcript']}`). "
            f"Stall lasted about {mins} min."
        )
    return (
        f"*Resolved: jadegate mayor is back on Fable* (`{c['model']}`, transcript `{c['transcript']}`). "
        f"Downgrade lasted about {mins} min."
    )


def cswap_seat():
    """One line naming the active cswap seat, e.g. 'Account-9 (a@b [Org]) [Max 20x - Fable] Fable 13%'.
    Read-only `cswap status`, bounded to 20 s; raises on any failure (the caller prints 'seat unknown')."""
    out = subprocess.run([CSWAP, "status"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20, check=True).stdout
    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in out.splitlines()]
    head = next(ln for ln in lines if ln.startswith("Status:"))
    seat = head[len("Status:"):].strip()
    fable = next((ln for ln in lines if "Fable:" in ln), None)
    if fable:
        m = re.search(r"Fable:\s*(\d+%)", fable)
        if m:
            seat += f" Fable {m.group(1)}"
    return seat


def _seat_or_unknown():
    try:
        return cswap_seat() or "seat unknown"
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 -- a hung or missing cswap must never hide the verdict
        log(f"SEAT-FAIL {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        return "seat unknown"


def _hhmm(ts):
    e = _epoch(ts)
    return time.strftime("%m-%d %H:%M", time.localtime(e)) if e is not None else "?"


def stall_action(sig):
    if sig == "ORG-DISABLED":
        return "cswap switch to a seat outside that org with Fable room; ask Afik for the word to disable that org's seats"
    if sig == "WALL":
        return ("DO-NOT 71/78: `cswap switch <n>` to a seat whose `cswap status --json` `scoped` carries a Fable pct with "
                "headroom, THEN `gc handoff`; never accept a Switch-to-Opus dialog, never `cswap disable/enable` (DO-NOT 74)")
    return "read the error text below; if the next turn dies the same way, cswap switch to another seat with Fable room and tell Afik"


def _stall_facts(c):
    s = c["stall"]
    return (
        f"{s['signature']}: {s['count']} consecutive API-error turns, {_hhmm(s['first_ts'])} to {_hhmm(s['last_ts'])} "
        f"(first {s['first_ts']}, last {s['last_ts']}). Active cswap seat now: {c.get('seat') or 'seat unknown'}. "
        f"Error text: \"{s['text']}\"."
    )


def stalled_alert_text(c, first):
    head = "*jadegate mayor STALLED*" if first else "*jadegate mayor still stalled*"
    return (
        f"{head} <@{AFIK}> -- every recent turn ends in an API error before a model answers, so crons and inbound are dying. "
        f"{_stall_facts(c)} Transcript `{c['transcript']}`. "
        f"Recommended: {stall_action(c['stall']['signature'])}. The watchdog changed nothing in cswap or the settings."
    )


def stalled_mail_text(c):
    return (
        f"Your recent turns ended in API errors before a model answered. {_stall_facts(c)} Transcript {c['transcript']}. "
        "If you are reading this, a turn completed: check `cswap status`, then look for prompts (crons, WeCom, Slack) "
        "that arrived during the window and died unanswered (DO-NOT 137). "
        f"Recommended: {stall_action(c['stall']['signature'])}. "
        "The watchdog changed nothing in cswap or the settings. This mail repeats hourly while the newest rows are still errors; "
        "#gastown has been alerted and will be told when it is resolved."
    )


def main(argv):
    dry = "--dry-run" in argv
    st = load_state()
    c = classify(st.get("state"), st.get("stall"))
    if "--model-only" in argv:
        print(c.get("model") or "unknown")
        return 0
    if "--status" in argv:
        print(json.dumps({**c, "saved_state": load_state()}, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False))
        return 0
    if "--announce" in argv:
        slack_post(
            f"Model watchdog armed on the jadegate mayor: polls the mayor transcript every 5 min for the model of the last turn "
            f"(currently `{c.get('model')}`). Downgrade to anything but Fable posts here + mails the mayor to hand off; "
            "recovery posts here too. Script `~/city/bin/mayor-model-watchdog`, launchd `com.jadegate.model-watchdog`.", dry)
        return 0

    prev = st.get("state", "OK")
    now = int(time.time())
    enforce_settings_flags(dry)  # every tick, idempotent
    if c["state"] == "UNKNOWN":
        log(f"UNKNOWN: {c.get('reason')}")
        return 0
    if c["state"] in BAD_STATES:
        kind = c["state"]
        stalled = kind == "STALLED"
        first = prev != kind
        due = first or now - st.get("last_alert", 0) >= REALERT_SECS
        # a stall is dated from its first error row, a downgrade from the tick that saw it
        began = (c["stall"].get("first_epoch") or now) if stalled else now
        # Record the verdict BEFORE any network call: on 2026-09-09 an exception inside slack_post
        # aborted the run before log/state/mail, so both real downgrades left no trace here.
        st.update({"state": kind, "model": c["model"], "since": began if first else st.get("since"),
                   "transcript": c["transcript"], "checked": now})
        if first:
            # a new verdict owes its own first alert: without this, a first alert whose channels both fail
            # would wait out the PREVIOUS verdict's last_alert (up to an hour) instead of retrying next tick
            st["last_alert"] = 0
            if prev in BAD_STATES:
                log(f"SUPERSEDED {prev} by {kind} (no resolved notice; the {kind} alert follows)")
        if stalled:
            st["stall"] = c["stall"]
        else:
            st.pop("stall", None)
        if not dry:
            save_state(st)
        if stalled:
            s = c["stall"]
            if c.get("held"):
                log(f"HOLD STALLED: recovery not confirmed (needs {RESOLVE_REAL_ROWS} trailing real rows, or one "
                    f"standing {RESOLVE_QUIET_SECS // 60} min with no error after it)")
            log(f"STALLED sig={s['signature']} errors={s['count']} first={s['first_ts']} last={s['last_ts']} "
                f"model={c['model']} transcript={c['transcript']} due={due}")
            if due:
                c["seat"] = _seat_or_unknown()  # read-only, bounded; no cswap/settings change on a stall (DO-NOT 74)
            subject = f"STALLED {s['signature']}: mayor's last {s['count']} turns died in API errors"
            mail_body, slack_body = (lambda: stalled_mail_text(c)), (lambda: stalled_alert_text(c, first))
        else:
            log(f"DOWNGRADED model={c['model']} transcript={c['transcript']} settings={c.get('settings_model')} due={due}")
            # Afik 2026-09-09 12:37 CST: "let it restore the field" -- idempotent, runs every downgraded tick.
            changed, old, backup = restore_settings_model(dry)
            c["restored"] = {"changed": changed, "old": old, "backup": backup}
            if changed and not dry:
                st["restored"] = {"at": now, "from": old, "to": FABLE_SETTING, "backup": backup}
                save_state(st)
            subject = f"MODEL DOWNGRADE: mayor on {c['model']} -- hand off to a fresh Fable session now"
            mail_body, slack_body = (lambda: mail_text(c)), (lambda: alert_text(c, first))
        if due:
            # Mail first (it reaches the actor who can fix it), Slack second; each channel isolated.
            mail_ok = _attempt("mail", lambda: mail_mayor(subject, mail_body(), dry))
            slack_ok = _attempt("slack", lambda: slack_post(slack_body(), dry))
            log(f"ALERT mail={'ok' if mail_ok else 'FAILED'} slack={'ok' if slack_ok else 'FAILED'}")
            if mail_ok or slack_ok:
                st["last_alert"] = now  # if both channels failed, retry at the next 5-min tick, not in an hour
    else:
        if prev in BAD_STATES:
            log(f"RESOLVED model={c['model']} after {now - (st.get('since') or now)}s was={prev}")
            since = st.get("since")
            slack_ok = _attempt("slack", lambda: slack_post(resolved_text(c, since, prev), dry))
            if not slack_ok:
                log("RESOLVED notice not posted to #gastown")
        st.update({"state": "OK", "model": c["model"], "since": None, "transcript": c["transcript"], "last_alert": st.get("last_alert", 0)})
        st.pop("stall", None)
        if prev not in BAD_STATES:
            log(f"OK model={c['model']} transcript={c['transcript']}")
    st["checked"] = now
    if not dry:
        save_state(st)
    return 0


def _attempt(name, fn):
    """Run one notification channel; log and swallow its failure so the others still run."""
    try:
        fn()
        return True
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 -- a dead channel must never hide the verdict
        log(f"ALERT-FAIL {name}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        return False


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
